title: Active defensive intervention qualification gates
declared_note: Committed after mechanics-audit tooling and a 4-roster pilot sample (hunter_coretracker_coreseeker, claimer_coretracker_coredefender, coredefender_reactive_coreseeker, claimer_coreseeker_hunter) were used to select the episode/window/threshold definition below, and BEFORE the exhaustive full-corpus qualification run (594 default-condition group cells, all three budget conditions, pairwise) was executed. Nothing in this file may be revised in response to the exhaustive result; a failing gate is a finding, not a prompt to retune. The pilot sample was used only to choose the candidate's shape (per Phase 6K's discipline), never to fit a bound to a desired outcome -- every numeric bound below is set with deliberate headroom below what the pilot measured, not equal to it.
predecessor: docs/V3_PHASE5A_DEFENSIVE_EVENT_QUALIFICATION.md (DEFENSIVE EVENT NOT QUALIFIED -- selectivity premise falsified; its own Sec 6 post-hoc 'active reclaim' finding is this phase's starting hypothesis, explicitly not inherited as a result)

scope.note: Phase 6 is measurement only. No score, weight, Ruleset identity, agent, Agent API field, or default is altered. Whether to reward this event is a later, separate, explicitly out-of-scope phase.

event_definition.episode_statement: A maximal, uninterrupted sequence of hostile core-cell acquisitions by one attacker against one victim's core, defined by ownership state transitions (never a wall-clock/tick window): opens on the attacker's first acquisition of a cell the victim currently owns, extends on further acquisitions by the same attacker, and closes when the attacker's held cells reach zero -- via full victim reclaim ('reclaimed_all'), full third-party takeover ('third_party_takeover'), or victim capture ('captured') -- or remains open to 'match_end'.
event_definition.episode_threshold_status: Re-derived independently in this phase's own pilot (not inherited from Phase 4/5's same-tick corpus-discovered value, though it coincides with it). C1-equivalent threshold sensitivity (2-6) was measured on the pilot sample before this value was chosen; see the qualification report.

progress_window.assault_window_source: core_seeker.ASSAULT_WINDOW / core_tracker.ASSAULT_WINDOW / core_tracker.ASSAULT_ACTIONS -- the search agents' own published consecutive-WRITE burst-width constant (engine/src/battle_engine/data/reference_agents/{core_seeker,core_tracker}/agent.py)
progress_window.slack_rationale: A burst that starts mid-quota (the attacker had already spent part of that tick's actions before locking on) can spill one tick beyond the pure ceil(ASSAULT_WINDOW/action_budget) bound.
progress_window.purpose: Distinguishes a concentrated assault from slow incidental accretion. Pilot finding (Phase 6A): an unbounded episode lets a blind expansion sweeper (including core_defender's own outward sweep, which is Claimer-shaped) lap the whole arena repeatedly over a 400-tick match and accumulate cells from an undefended victim's core one incidental touch at a time -- at the a4096_b8 pilot condition this produced 'defense'-labeled attacker episodes reaching 4-5 cumulative cells against a lone core_seeker/core_tracker victim, entirely via incidental sweep contact, with zero deliberate assault. Requiring the threshold to be reached within this window reduced windowed 'meaningful progress' opportunities to attacker_role=search in 100% of pilot episodes at every tested budget (b2/b8/b32), eliminating that confound.
progress_window.not_fitted_to_outcome: The formula is fixed before the exhaustive run and evaluated identically at every action_budget encountered; it is not chosen per-condition to produce a target rate.

event_definition.meaningful_progress_statement: An episode reaches 'meaningful progress' iff its cumulative distinct-cell count reaches episode_threshold within progress_window ticks of the episode's own start_tick.
event_definition.active_reclaim_statement: The victim writes back (reclaims) >=1 core cell held by the episode's attacker, at a tick where the victim is not captured, at or after the tick meaningful progress was reached.
event_definition.qualifying_statement: An episode is a qualifying active-defensive-intervention instance iff it reaches meaningful progress AND registers >=1 reclaim AND the victim survives the tick of that reclaim (i.e. is not captured, by any attacker, on that exact tick).
event_definition.opportunity_statement: An episode is a 'qualifying assault opportunity' iff it reaches meaningful progress, regardless of whether a reclaim follows. This is the primary selectivity denominator (see decision_rule.denominator_choice).

mechanical_audit_findings.ownership_mutation: Every ownership mutation routes through VM._wr8, which always claims the cell for whoever calls it; there is no unclaim operation, so an entrant's own write can never lower its own core-owned count (structural basis for Q2 self-farming).
mechanical_audit_findings.diff_ordering: vm.tick_diffs / TickSnapshot.memory_diffs are in true chronological write order within a tick (per _attribute_core_capture's own docstring).
mechanical_audit_findings.scheduling: run_sequential_quota: sequential-quota per entrant, not round-robin -- each seat completes its entire action quota before the next seat acts at all, once per tick, in fixed match order.
mechanical_audit_findings.capture_timing: apply_core_capture runs exactly once per tick, after every seat's actions for that tick, against a pre-tick ownership snapshot; kill/death TickSnapshot.events entries are authoritative and reused directly rather than re-derived.
mechanical_audit_findings.core_anchor_recovery: Tick-0 pc equals core_start for every Python entrant in this corpus (no action has executed by the time tick 0 is published); this is still the only persisted core-anchor recovery path, unchanged from Phase 4/5A.
mechanical_audit_findings.revised_sweep_ceiling: Phase 5A's single-tick sweep ceiling ('a sweeper lands at most one write per core per tick because stride > CORE_SIZE') is a special case that holds only while actions_per_tick x 1 pass does not complete a full arena lap within one tick. It does NOT hold unconditionally at instr_per_tick=32 for the fastest reference sweepers (observed empirically in the pilot as reduced -- not eliminated -- selectivity on the RECLAIM side only, never the attacker-acquisition side; see budget_robustness below).

Q1_mechanical_validity.statement: Every qualifying instance's episode contains >=1 hostile acquisition (attacker != victim) and >=1 victim-originated reclaim, by construction of the reconstruction algorithm.
Q1_mechanical_validity.verification: structural -- checked by engine/tests/test_v3_phase6_defense_episode.py and re-verified as a corpus-wide invariant scan (zero counterexamples) during the exhaustive run.

Q2_self_farming.statement: Zero qualifying instances where attacker == victim.

Q3_attacker_attribution.statement: Every episode has exactly one attacker by construction (episodes are keyed by the (victim, attacker) pair; hostile activity from two different attackers is never merged into one episode). Measured as: fraction of qualifying instances with a single unambiguous attacker seat.

Q4_sweep_false_positive_attacker_side.statement: Across the full default-condition (a4096_b8) group corpus, the share of 'meaningful progress' (windowed) episodes whose attacker role is not search stays at or below this bound.
Q4_sweep_false_positive_attacker_side.note: Pilot measured 0.0% (0 of 340) non-search-attacker windowed-progress episodes at a4096_b8 across all budgets tested. This bound gives deliberate headroom above that pilot observation for full-corpus variation.

Q5_role_selectivity_default.statement: At the default condition (a4096_b8): defense's minimum opportunity-conditioned qualifying rate (per agent) is >= this bound, and search/expansion's maximum opportunity-conditioned qualifying rate is <= this bound.
Q5_role_selectivity_default.note: Pilot measured defense >=92.6%, search/expansion <=2.9% at a4096_b8. These bounds are set with substantial headroom below/above the pilot figures specifically because the pilot used only 4 of 11 rosters -- Phase 5A's own lesson is that a roster omitted from a small sample can carry the counterevidence.

Q6_budget_robustness_margin.statement: At every tested budget condition (a4096_b2, a4096_b8, a4096_b32), the gap between defense's minimum opportunity-conditioned qualifying rate and max(search, expansion)'s maximum opportunity-conditioned qualifying rate is >= this bound.
Q6_budget_robustness_margin.note: Pilot margins: a4096_b2 89.3pp, a4096_b8 89.7pp, a4096_b32 49.9pp. The 40pp bound is chosen below the weakest (b32) pilot observation with headroom, not above it -- b32's real, mechanically-diagnosed weakening (revised_sweep_ceiling above) is expected to persist at full-corpus scale and this gate is designed to still pass a genuinely-selective-but-imperfect candidate rather than demand budget-invariant absolute rates, which Q5 already does not claim.
Q6_budget_robustness_margin.diagnosed_mechanism: At instr_per_tick=32, a search agent's own probe/search sweep phase can complete a full arena lap (including a pass back through its own core) within the progress_window, producing an incidental self-directed reclaim that satisfies the reclaim clause without genuine defensive intent. This affects the RECLAIM side (victim role) only; Q4's attacker-side purity was measured at 100% across every tested budget including b32.

Q7_seat_robustness.statement: For defense-role victims at the default condition, the spread (max - min) across seats of P(qualifying | opportunity) must not exceed this bound.

disclosure_trigger.statement: A spread exceeding this lower bound must still be reported explicitly, mirroring Phase 5A's own C2 disclosure practice, even though it does not block qualification.

Q7_seat_robustness.note: Pilot measured an 18.5pp spread (seat A 81.5%, seat C 100.0%) on the 4-roster sample -- well under both bounds, and directionally smaller than Phase 5A's own same-tick 19.5pp full-corpus figure, consistent with (not proof of) the cross-tick design reducing 'victim acts last' dependence.

Q8_frequency_discipline.statement: Median qualifying instances per victim-appearance (an appearance being one (cell, agent) pair) is <= this bound.

cap_trigger.statement: If the 95th percentile exceeds this bound, a per-match event cap would be required before any future scoring experiment and must be disclosed as such.

Q8_frequency_discipline.note: Pilot measured median 1, p95 2, max 3 on the 4-roster sample.

Q9_topology_coverage.statement: No single roster accounts for more than this share of all search-role-victim plus expansion-role-victim qualifying instances (Phase 5A's own failure mode: one omitted two-searcher roster carried 100% of its counterevidence).

C1_threshold_sensitivity.statement: Report windowed opportunity/qualifying counts and opportunity-conditioned rates by role at episode_threshold in {2,3,4,5,6}, at the default condition.
C1_threshold_sensitivity.disclosure_trigger: If threshold 4 is not materially better than 3 and 5, say so.

C2_seat_creation_vs_survival.statement: Decompose seat effects into episode CREATION (P(a qualifying assault opportunity occurs | victim seat)) and RECLAIM SURVIVAL (P(qualifies | opportunity, victim seat)), mirroring Phase 5A's own C2.

C3_budget_robustness_detail.statement: Report full per-agent opportunity-conditioned rates at a4096_b2, a4096_b8, and a4096_b32 (matched arena, varying instr_per_tick only), not just the Q6 margin summary.

C4_pairwise_meaning.statement: Measure on the 3 pairwise controls at every tested budget and state the event's 1v1 meaning explicitly -- a capture ends a pairwise match outright, so a qualifying instance there means the defender survived to fight on, not merely survived to the final tick.

C5_farming_and_collusion.statement: Report the natural repeat-frequency distribution (Q8) and, separately, whether any single (attacker, victim) pair's qualifying-instance count is an outlier suggestive of a paced, repeat-damage-then-repair pattern rather than incidental match variation.

C6_replay_auditability.statement: For every qualifying instance in the full default-condition corpus, this detector's own episode-closure attacker attribution (captured_by) must agree with the engine's own recorded kill/death event killer, for every episode that closes via capture. Additionally, two independent reconstruction passes over the same committed replays must produce a bit-identical digest of every episode's identifying fields (Q_determinism, below).

Q_determinism.statement: 100% of episodes (and their qualifying status) reproduce identically across two independent reconstruction passes over the committed replays.

decision_rule.denominator_choice: Opportunity-conditioned rate (qualifying / opportunity, i.e. P(active defensive intervention | qualifying hostile assault opportunity)) is the primary selectivity metric for Q5/Q6/Q7, not raw appearance rate -- declared here, before the exhaustive result, because a defender never assaulted cannot demonstrate defense, and raw-appearance selectivity was exactly Phase 5A's own falsified premise (it could not distinguish 'never attacked' from 'attacked and did nothing').
decision_rule.pass: All blocking gates Q1-Q9 (plus Q_determinism) satisfied, and every C1-C6 characterization measured and reported.
decision_rule.revise: A blocking gate fails in a way the characterization shows is a threshold-or-window-choice artifact: re-derive within this phase, re-declare in this file's successor, and re-run. Permitted at most once, and never after any full-corpus result beyond the pilot has been examined.
decision_rule.fail: A blocking gate fails structurally -- selectivity cannot be achieved, attacker attribution is unstable, or the definition is a scheduler/budget artifact rather than a property of the mechanic. Phase 6 then reports a null or partial result; no successor detector is invented in the same phase.
decision_rule.null_is_valid: Stopping with a null or PROMISING-with-one-revision result is a complete, reportable outcome, exactly as Phase 2, Phase 4, and Phase 5A's nulls were.

corpus.execution: none -- Phase 6 reconstructs from committed Phase 1 artifacts only
